summary: Kungu territory (Sud-Ubangi) in north-western DRC, comprising the Kungu, Boto and Bokonzi areas between Gemena and the Ubangi river, lies far from the eastern conflict zones. The last significant armed episode in the territory was the 2009-2010 Enyele/Dongo insurgency (Ubangi river side, around Dongo), which was put down by FARDC/PNC with MONUSCO support; no armed group is known to hold territory here since. Towns and villages are administered by the territorial administration and customary chiefs, with PNC posts as the main force maintaining order; insecurity consists of ordinary crime and local/customary disputes. Web search was unavailable in this run (search budget exhausted, other engines blocked), so this assessment rests on default state presence and general knowledge.

zones.description: Larger towns of Kungu territory (>=10,000 people: e.g. Bonduni, Mbenga, Bogbozo, Gemena (Kungu), Couvent, Isabe, Boyangba)
zones.evidence: No reported armed-group presence or parallel authority in Kungu territory since the suppression of the 2009-2010 Enyele/Dongo insurgency; PNC posts and territorial administration maintain order. Not verified with recent sources in this run.
